finding: V2 caught the reference model answering 'Which came first, the Fenn commissioning or the Yarrow move?' with real knowledge about Yarrow Shipbuilders' 1900s move to Scotstoun. A sweep of every entity bank found 75 of 163 names are real-world referents.
harm_model: A real referent is only exploitable where its real-world facts answer the question asked. 'Meridian Tools' being a real brand does not tell a model which vendor the USER chose; 'Yarrow' being a shipbuilder that moved in 1906 does tell it which milestone came first. Harm therefore concentrates in ORDERING questions, where the referent carries a date.
v2_undercounts_this: V2 scores only a leak that AGREES with gold. Five temporal questions show world-knowledge reasoning; V2 flagged two. tme-tem-013 hit 10/10 because the corpus happened to order those events the way history did -- ordered the other way the model would have been confidently wrong ten times and the question would have PASSED. The arm that caught this cannot certify the fix.

declared_not_remediated.reason: Measured and assessed low-harm: these names are vendors, places someone lived, products chosen, or people's first names in padding. None answers its question. Rewriting them would move all nine corpus shas and reset every control the consuming project holds, for no measured leak. Declared rather than silently rewritten.
